newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: KEMP DEFENDS GOVT'S JOBS GROWTH
Federal Education and Training Minister David Kemp there is jobs growth, despite the release of the latest ANZ job advertisements figures.
The series fell by a seasonally adjusted one-point-nine per cent in March, with just more than 19-thousand positions advertised.
Dr Kemp says vacancies fluctuate from month to month, but concedes more jobs growth is needed.
AWU ACCUSES BHP OF WINDING DOWN AUSTRALIAN STEEL OPERATIONS
The Australian Workers Union, in its submission to the National Parliamentary steel industry inquiry, has accused BHP of gradually winding down its steelmaking operations in Australia.
The Union believes BHP is investing money offshore while neglecting its operations back home.
The Union says all of the capital BHP now makes out of it's steel making operations in Australia is being invested in South east asia and in the U-S.
It says BHP is prepared to wind down its steel making plant in Newcastle due to its high operating costs, but has accused BHP of deliberately inflating the Steelwork's operating costs.
INDONESIAN TRADE OFFICIALS TO INSPECT BEEF SAFETY
Senior Indonesian trade officials are expected in Sydney later this week to inspect beef safety procedures.
The New South Wales Government has invited the officials in an effort to convince them that beef from this state is safe.
Last week Indonesia extended its ban on New South Wales beef for another three-weeks.
It's also imposed a 12-month ban on beef from properties where there have been anthrax outbreaks.
New South Wales Agriculture Minister, Richard Amery, says the bans should be lifted.
MILAT'S APPEAL
Negotiations will be held over the next fortnight to finalise the legal representation of backpacker killer, Ivan Milat.
Milat, who serving a life terms for the murder of seven backpackers, is appealing to the Court of Criminal Appeal.
The grounds for the appeal have yet to be determined.
New South Wales' highest court today adjourned the matter for later this month, to allow Brisbane-based lawyer Andrew Boe and the Legal Aid Commission to discuss the representation of Milat.
TELSTRA DENIES TIMED CALL CHARGES
Telstra has emphatically denied it intends introducing timed call charges for use of the internet.
Telstra's John Rowland says Internet Service Providers and their customers should disregard what he calls misinformation about timed calls.
Mr Rowland says the 1997 legislation requires that Telstra continue to provide residential customers with untimed calls.
He says he can only reiterate that Telstra has no plans to introduce timed call charges for Internet Service Providers.
HOWARD SAYS NO CUTS TO MEDICAL RESEARCH FUNDING
Prime Minister John Howard has used today's opening of the Garvan Institute's new building in Sydney, to pledge there'll be no cutbacks in medical research funding in the May Federal Budget.
Mr Howard said despite cutbacks to other areas in the last budget, the Federal Government increased expenditure on medical research.
He said that won't change in the May budget, saying that medical research is something that should always receive the enthusiastic support of government.
NEW BOOK HOPES TO IMPROVE IMAGE OF CLERGY
The Catholic Church says a new book, which contains stories of several peoples' relationships with their priests, will highlight the extraordinary relationship between a priest and his people.
Catholic Church Spokesman, Father Mark Coleridge says the book, called "Clay in the Potters Hand", is a testimonial to the heroic and often unsung work of ordinary priests in the community.
He says the stories in the book relate the very human face of the priesthood.
Father Coleridge says he hopes the book will go some way to improving public perception of the clergy.
